extracted.intended_audience: readers of realist literary fiction and writers studying characterization and narrative craft
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting character-driven realist fiction that uses social detail, dialogue, and authorial commentary to reveal motive, class, and moral complexity. Emphasizes showing characters through action/objects and balancing scene with reflective analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization through action, objects, and setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal character by what they do and the things around them (e.g., San Giacinto's room: 'Papers were tied together...the big inkstand was just in the middle...', Orsino studying the tapestry, the butler offering wines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, specific details—rooms, furniture, possessions, habitual gestures and small acts at table or club—to make personalities visible rather than simply telling the reader. Examples in the text: the precise ordering of San Giacinto's desk conveys his temperament; Orsino's impatience and gambling show his restlessness. Anti-pattern: generic adjectives without situational specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show internal states by juxtaposing external behavior and inner thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast what characters outwardly do (polite dinner talk, smiles, polite replies about theatre) with their private responses and reflections (Orsino's boredom, Sant' Ilario's inward comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place scenes of social mask next to interior narration or free indirect thought to reveal hypocrisy, constraint, or longing. Use small telling gestures (a look, a turn to tapestry) to cue inner life. Avoid flattening characters by keeping only one register (solely external or solely internal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of authorial social commentary to provide causal depth
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator steps back to analyze wider social causes (e.g., 'It is of no use to deny the enormous influence of brandy and games of chance on the men of the present day...'), linking individual vice to social conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ occasional authorial reflection to situate characters within broader social, economic, or psychological forces. These passages should illuminate motive and context without entirely substituting for scene work. Anti-pattern: long moralizing paragraphs that shut down character ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray vice as a process, not an instant label
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit thematic claim in the text: 'Vice begins when the excitement ceases to be a matter of taste and turns into a necessity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatize the gradual transition from pastime to dependency rather than presenting characters as innately 'bad.' Show early amusement, escalating need, and eventual compulsion. Use incremental incidents (first wins, then losses, increased drinking, borrowing) to chart the arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define character aims clearly (occupation vs. excitement) to motivate choices
rubrics_metrics.description: San Giacinto teases apart Orsino's motives: 'You therefore wish one or more of three things--money for its own sake, excitement or occupation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the protagonist's desire explicit in the text (even if disputed) so that their decisions can be read as attempts to satisfy identifiable needs. Use other characters' diagnoses (practical counsel, skeptic relatives) to sharpen and test those aims. Anti-pattern: vague 'I want something' without hints as to what it actually is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast generations to reveal thematic conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Generational quarrels are used to expose themes: the old prince's view of aging and tradition vs Orsino's dread of a dull inherited life ('we all turn into the same shape at seventy...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage family or generational interactions where older characters embody tradition and younger characters yearn for change. Use repeated motifs (dinner, lectures, jokes) to show the persistence of values and the younger characters' reactions to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic, pragmatic dialogue that carries exposition and moral outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters speak in utilitarian, personality-revealing ways (San Giacinto's businesslike advice, Sant' Ilario's paterfamilias counsel), letting dialogue deliver character and argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write dialogue that accomplishes multiple functions: reveals character voice, advances plot, and conveys argument or world-view. Avoid stilted 'information-dump' speeches; instead let conversational tone, interruptions, and prop-based gestures keep it lifelike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific occupational and economic detail for authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground scenes in realistic jobs, financial practices and consequences (references to 'government bonds', 'mortgages', building speculation, the carpenter/tobacconist/mason example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate, specific details about professions, finance, and practical steps to lend credibility to characters' plans and mistakes. These details can also function as thematic material (e.g., speculation as pseudo-occupation). Avoid vague generalities about 'business' or 'work.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance scene action with reflective analysis (pacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative alternates between immediate action (dinner, cards, dealing, the winning/losing sequence) and longer reflective passages about social causes and the nature of vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modulate rhythm by mixing vivid scenes with short analytic paragraphs that broaden perspective; ensure reflective sections illuminate rather than stall the story. Monitor length and placement so introspection deepens stakes rather than diluting momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish stakes through concrete consequences and choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Orsino's gamble leads to tangible outcomes (fifteen thousand francs, plans for building speculation, potential borrowing), making his desires consequential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor a character's yearning in measurable consequences—money gained or lost, relationships strained, social position altered—so reader investment grows from the practical risks as well as emotional aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contrast and irony to modulate tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator and characters frequently employ ironic remarks (old prince's lampooning of dinner guests, comments about Montevarchi's fortunes) to shade social critique with humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply gentle or cutting irony to reveal character judgments and to prevent sentimentalizing. Irony can both entertain and sharpen moral observation; be careful that it does not undercut necessary empathy for characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make advice and counsel dramatic rather than didactic
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel scenes (San Giacinto advising Orsino, Sant' Ilario's mixed tolerance) are dramatized—tied to relationships and power dynamics—rather than delivered as abstract lectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characters give advice, embed it in conflict, tone, and gesture so it serves plot and characterization. Avoid flat authorial injunctions; let other characters' reactions reveal the advice's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use material culture to mark social standing and temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated reference to objects and rituals (opera boxes 'when the piece was not on the Index', wines, tapestry, portrait of Flavia) signals class habits and preoccupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select culturally specific items and habits that distinguish families and social circles. Objects should do narrative work—hinting at taste, pretension, memory, or constraint—rather than merely decorating scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray decision-making as a function of temperament and circumstance
rubrics_metrics.description: Orsino's impulsive moves—gambling, sudden plan to speculate—are presented as the interplay of his temperament ('He loved excitement') and social circumstances (boredom, availability of winnings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how personality traits combine with external pressures to produce choices; this avoids simplistic moralizing and allows dramatic irony when characters misread their own motives.
